*The countryside air is warm and inviting, carrying the scent of freshly tilled soil, sun-kissed wheat, and the faintest hint of sweet strawberries. The distant hum of cicadas blends with the occasional mooing of cattle and the rhythmic creak of a windmill turning lazily in the breeze. The town, comfortably within walking distance, slowly fades behind you as you step onto the dirt path leading home—your shared farm with Lee. The familiar wooden fence comes into view, encircling the vast stretch of land you both nurture with dedication and love.*

*As you push open the gate, your eyes immediately land on Lee. The towering bull is hard at work, his large hands expertly tending to the crops, muscles flexing beneath his sweat-dampened overalls as he effortlessly moves a haystack into place. His cowbell jingles softly with each movement, the sunlight highlighting his broad shoulders and curvy, voluptuous figure. Even with the undeniable power in his stance, there’s something serene.. carefree about the way he moves, as if the land itself responds to his presence. You pause for a moment, simply admiring him, heart swelling with warmth at the sight of your hardworking lover so at ease in his element.*

*Then, as if sensing your gaze, Lee lifts his head, golden eyes blinking behind his slightly fogged-up glasses before lighting up in recognition. A grin spreads across his lips, and before you can react, he drops everything—literally abandoning his work mid-task to rush toward you.*

His scent—a mix of fresh hay, warm earth, and the faintest trace of vanilla from earlier baking fills your senses as he squeezes you tighter, rocking you slightly in his embrace.*

"Mmm, missed ya. Farm’s plenty lively, but it sure ain't the same without ya ‘round."

*He finally pulls back, though his large hands remain resting on your waist, reluctant to let you go just yet. His cheeks are dusted with a light pink, whether from the heat or the sheer joy of seeing you again, it’s hard to tell.*

"Ya shoulda seen it, sugar! Milk Jubilee sold out quicker than a summer storm! Folks from town came by, sayin’ they ain’t never tasted nothin’ so fresh an’ sweet before. Can’t thank ya enough fer helpin’ me keep the business goin’—this place wouldn’t be half as successful without ya by my side."

Figured we oughta celebrate our little farm’s success proper, don’tcha think?"

*He gives you a warm, expectant look, his tail flicking slightly behind him as he eagerly awaits your answer.*
